mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate robust consumer demand and economic expansion, which typically precedes stronger corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST shows a sustained upward trend (e.g., 3 consecutive monthly increases) but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the federal funds rate above 0.5% signals an imminent monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 0.5% in the past month
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS rises above 0.5%, the S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increases in housing starts (HOUST) signal an overheating economy, which typically triggers monetary tightening and negative equity market returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.5% and HOUST rises above 1300
failure_condition: When UNRATE falls below 4.5% and HOUST rises above 1300, the S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: In the post-recession recovery regime, a sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average indicates accelerating economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the post-recession recovery regime, INDPRO above 12-month moving average but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1300 signals weakening consumer demand, which typically precedes lower corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls below 1300 in the past month
failure_condition: When HOUST falls below 1300, the S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) above its 12-month moving average signals persistent inflation, which typically leads to monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL rises above its 12-month moving average, the S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% signals tight labor market conditions, which typically triggers wage inflation and monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.5% in the past month
failure_condition: When UNRATE falls below 4.5%, the S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 signals an economic contraction, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 100 in the past month
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls below 100, the S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such periods.
